purpose: Strengthens the SPK-13 pixel-parity acceptance from a single 256x256 / devicePixelRatio-1 window to an aspect+DPR matrix, so that a viewport- or projection-shape asymmetry cannot hide behind one constant canvas geometry.
strictRule: Unchanged from spk13-pixel-parity-20261012.json: every RGBA8 channel byte difference must be 0, both sides non-empty, each side stable against its own repeat, zero JS + drained GL errors, identical context attributes and unmasked renderer inside one engine, source/asset digest unchanged during the run, negative control must move pixels. No tolerance, no masks.

harnessFinding.discoveredBy: this matrix (DPR=2 columns); invisible to the earlier 256x256 / DPR-1 run
harnessFinding.symptom: First DPR=2 sweep: 3/3 engines FAIL with channelMismatch 983560/1048576 (94% of channels) while both sides were internally stable, and the reference image was a 2x magnified crop of the target. Preserved un-relabelled at docs/evidence/spark/spk13-pixel-parity-viewport-dpr2-before-unit-fix-20261012.json (passed=false; original collector path output/spark-pixel-parity-viewport-square-dpr2.json).
harnessFinding.rootCause: Collector-side unit mismatch, NOT an engine or SDK defect: the target reports its native gfx viewport in DEVICE pixels, while three.js WebGLRenderer.setViewport/setScissor take CSS pixels and multiply by the renderer pixel ratio internally (dist/three-reference.js:15570 and :17621-17622, read-only port repo). At devicePixelRatio 1 the two unit systems coincide, which is why the single-window run could not expose it.
harnessFinding.fix: tools/debug/probes/spark-pixel-parity/frame.js adopt() now divides the adopted viewport/scissor by DPR before calling the reference renderer; the target side is untouched.
harnessFinding.fixVerifiedBy: output/spark-pixel-parity-viewport-smoke-dpr2.json (chromium, channelMismatch=0, negative control 0 -> 957666) and the four DPR=2/DPR=1 windows re-collected in this file.

artifactProof.note: PNG files are the direct RGBA8 read-back re-encoded deterministically (same writer, row-flip only), so identical pixels mean identical file bytes.
artifactProof.reading: after-target == after-reference (parity reached) and before-target == after-target (the fix touched only the reference collector, never the engine path); before-reference is the odd one out (the 2x zoom).

discardedRuns.cause: Self-inflicted: this session edited the plan file while that window was running, and that file is one of the collector fingerprintFiles (drift assertion), so the run rejected itself. All 12 pixel rows were PASS; it is replaced by output/spark-pixel-parity-final-square-dpr1-02.json (drift=0). Kept un-relabelled as the record of the first attempt.

notClaimed: Not a cross-GPU/device generalisation: evidence binds to the three browser builds and this machine GPU listed in windows[].engines and .gpu.
Not release READY: the spark-rs crate-level licence disposition is still `pending` in docs/license-decisions.json, and the spark variant bundle is therefore not a published artifact.
The 5 window reports record a source/asset digest taken inside their own run; the evidence file itself and the ledger entries written afterwards are by construction outside that digest.
Camera-matrix construction parity is covered by SPK-04 math parity, not here (the reference adopts the target matrices).
